# SOC 2 Status Letter - Draft

Northfield asked for this after the term sheet. It goes in the data room by 2026-10-12. Signed by me as SOC 2 executive sponsor. Sam to fact-check every number before it goes out. No spin: Elena will compare it against SOC 2 Readiness Review - September line by line.

[Things I must NOT write: that we have a Type II report. We don't. The window is still open.]

---

**To:** Northfield Ventures (attn. Ravi Menon, Elena Sorensen)
**From:** Maya Chen, CTO and co-founder, Stencil
**Date:** October TK, 2026
**Re:** SOC 2 status

Ravi, Elena,

This letter summarizes where Stencil stands on SOC 2 as of early October 2026.

**Type I.** Ledgerwise Assurance issued our SOC 2 Type I report on June 30, 2026. The opinion was unqualified, with two observations. Both observations have been addressed; details are in SOC 2 Type I Report Summary. [Sam: confirm both observations are actually closed, not "in progress". If one isn't, say so.]

**Type II.** Our Type II observation window runs July 1 through December 31, 2026. We expect the report from Ledgerwise in Q1 2027 [TK confirm timing with Ledgerwise].

**Readiness review.** On September 10 we ran an internal readiness review against the Type II controls. It found three gaps. Current status of each:

1. *Quarterly access reviews.* Our Q3 user access review was late. As of this week it is 70% complete and due to finish October 10. We have changed the procedure so the Q4 review starts on the first business day of the quarter's last month rather than after quarter close (Access Review Procedure). [Sam: is that the actual change? I think so.]
2. *Vendor risk assessments.* Four vendors were missing current risk assessments. Two are complete (DriveWealth and Lithic, see Vendor Risk Assessment - DriveWealth and Vendor Risk Assessment - Lithic). The remaining two are due October 24.
3. *Endpoint management.* MDM coverage was 88% of company laptops at the readiness review. It is 96% today, and the remaining devices are scheduled for October 17 (MDM Rollout Plan).

We consider all three gaps remediable within the observation window. The access review gap will likely appear as an exception for Q3 in the Type II report; we would rather tell you that now than have you read it in March.

**Incidents during the window.** On September 26 we had a SEV1 incident in which 1,412 users were double-debited by a round-up sweep job. It was detected in 47 minutes, reversed the same day, and reported to our sponsor bank within 24 hours. The incident is documented in Postmortem - Sep 26 Duplicate Round-up Debits and was handled under our Incident Response Policy. Our auditors will see it as part of the window.

**People.** Sam Whitfield (security & compliance engineer, joined June 2026) runs the program day to day. I am executive sponsor. Hana Ito owns the BSA/AML program, which is separate from SOC 2 scope but reviewed alongside it.

Happy to walk through any of this on the October 14 call.

Maya Chen

---

## Before sending
- [ ] Sam: fact-check numbers and the Type I observation status by 2026-10-10
- [ ] Sam: confirm Q3 access review actually hits 100% by 2026-10-10, update line 1
- [ ] Hana: read the incident paragraph by 2026-10-11 (anything we say here, Pillar could see)
- [ ] Aleks: tone pass by 2026-10-11
- [ ] Upload to data room by 2026-10-12

Open question: do we name the auditor's expected exception at all? Leaning yes. Surprises are worse.
Risk: if Q3 access review isn't done by 10/10, this letter gets less true every day it sits there.
